Congressman Fuller Votes to Pass National Defense Authorization Act | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Votes to Pass National Defense Authorization Act July 22, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. Today, Congressman Fuller voted for H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, which funds the pay raise President Trump requested for America's service members and authorizes $1.1 trillion for national defense. The NDAA authorizes funding for the Department of Defense and national security programs.  “I know what we ask of the young men and women who serve, and I know what their families give up while they are gone. Paying them what they have earned is not a favor. It is the minimum, and yet the Democrats continue to refuse to support them,” said Congressman Fuller. “A strong national defense is essential, and we cannot let the radical left continue to put American citizens at risk.” 205 House Democrats voted against the bill, and against the pay raise inside it. The FY2027 NDAA backs the President's proposed pay increase for every rank, with the largest raises going to junior enlisted troops. Congressman Fuller will continue to fight for our service members and their families each and every day. Issues : Congress Economy Media Press Releases In the News Back to top button

Congressman Fuller Awarded “Hero of Main Street” by National Retail Federation | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Awarded “Hero of Main Street” by National Retail Federation July 16, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Fuller has been named a 2026 Hero of Main Street by the National Retail Federation, or NRF, for his support of the small businesses and Main Street employers that power the nation's economy. The award, presented at NRF's annual Retail Advocates Summit in Washington, recognizes members of Congress who stand up for retailers and the communities they serve. "I am honored to accept this recognition, but this award belongs to the small business owners of Northwest Georgia who open their doors, make payroll, and keep our towns running. I will keep fighting to get Washington off their backs and give them the freedom to grow," said Congressman Fuller. The National Retail Federation is the world's largest retail trade association, and retail businesses employ over 62,200 Northwest Georgians. Small businesses are the backbone of America, and Congressman Fuller continues to prioritize those foundations that keep Northwest Georgia strong. Congressman Fuller Votes to Block Financial Surveillance of Lawful Gun Owners | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Votes to Block Financial Surveillance of Lawful Gun Owners July 15, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C.  - Congressman Fuller voted to pass the Protecting Privacy in Purchases Act, barring payment card networks from tagging firearms retailers with special merchant codes that would let banks and credit card companies track lawful gun and ammunition purchases. The bill passed the House this evening and now moves to the Senate. “The government has no business building a list of who buys a firearm and who buys ammunition. That is a backdoor gun registry, and every gun owner in Northwest Georgia should be free of it. As the District Attorney for the Lookout Mountain Judicial Circuit, I spent my career protecting law-abiding citizens, not tracking them,” said Congressman Fuller. This legislation is crucial to prevent credit card issuers from singling out firearm retailers, and it directs the Department of Justice to enforce the ban and report to Congress each year on the resulting investigations. Congressman Fuller Keeps Promise of Opening Two New Offices in Northwest Georgia | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Keeps Promise of Opening Two New Offices in Northwest Georgia August 20, 2026 Press Release NORTHWEST GEORGIA — Congressman Fuller promised the hardworking people of Northwest Georgia that he would open two new district offices to better serve constituents across Georgia’s 14th Congressional District. Today, that promise is fulfilled.. Opening these two new offices in Rome and Dallas, two of the most populated cities in Georgia’s 14th Congressional District, will make it easier for constituents across the district to access their congressional office and receive assistance with casework, Social Security, VA services, and other federal matters. This expansion reflects Congressman Fuller’s commitment to being accessible, responsive, and transparent, and ensuring the people of Northwest Georgia have a strong and accessible advocate in Congress. The new district offices are located at the addresses below and will be open during the following hours of operation: Dallas District Office Paulding County Watson Government Complex - Located on the second floor. 240 Constitution Boulevard, Dallas, Georgia 30132 Open Mondays and Tuesdays, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Rome District Office Floyd County Administrative Building- Located on the second floor. 12 East 4th Ave, Rome, Georgia 30161 Open Wednesdays and Thursdays, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Our Dalton district office remains fully operational and will be open during the following hours of operation: Dalton District Office 702 South Thornton Ave, P.O. Box 829, Dalton, Georgia 30722 Open Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. “I am proud to officially open two new district offices for the hardworking people of Georgia’s 14th Congressional District. My team and I are committed to being there for our constituents, and these offices will allow us to be more accessible and better serve communities across Northwest Georgia. I am honored to fulfill my promise to expand our constituent services throughout the district and ensure we are putting the people of Georgia’s 14th District firs

Congressman Fuller Votes to Pass the Main Street Act for Northwest Georgia’s Hometown Banks | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Votes to Pass the Main Street Act for Northwest Georgia’s Hometown Banks July 21, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. Congressman Fuller today voted to pass H.R. 6955, the Main Street Capital Access Act, which changes federal banking rules to increase access to capital at the local level and ensures that community lenders can focus on serving families, small businesses, and local economies, making life more affordable for Americans while empowering Main Street. The House passed the bill 270 to 155. "Greater access to capital allows small businesses to grow and create more jobs. I'm working to make Northwest Georgia's economy the most vibrant it can possibly be, and it starts with strengthening our community banks," said Congressman Fuller. Congressman Fuller remains determined to be a fighter for Main Street each and every day in Washington. Issues : Congress Economy Media Press Releases In the News Back to top button

Congressman Fuller Urges Federal Action to Secure Clean Drinking Water in Northwest Georgia | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Urges Federal Action to Secure Clean Drinking Water in Northwest Georgia June 22, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. — This week, Congressman Fuller highlighted the urgent public health and infrastructure challenges facing Northwest Georgia by sending letters to members of the Appropriations Committee urging enhanced federal funding to address PFAS contamination in local drinking water systems. In a letter to Representative Mike Simpson, Chairman of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies, Congressman Fuller emphasized the need for sustained investment in water treatment infrastructure, including support for a major project in the City of Summerville. "Clean drinking water is a basic expectation that every Northwest Georgian should be able to count on. The high levels of contamination found in our drinking water are completely unacceptable. My team and I have been fighting alongside our colleagues on the Appropriations Committee to secure the funding needed to eliminate these harmful forever chemicals from our communities. As a cancer survivor myself, this fight is deeply personal. I will not back down until every family in Georgia's 14th Congressional District has access to clean, safe drinking water," said Congressman Fuller. Congressman Fuller remains committed to working at the federal, state, and local levels to deliver long-term solutions that protect public health and ensure every family in Northwest Georgia has access to clean, safe drinking water. Congressman Fuller Introduces the SHIELD Citizens Act, Requiring U.S. Citizenship for Federal Welfare Programs | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Introduces the SHIELD Citizens Act, Requiring U.S. Citizenship for Federal Welfare Programs July 15, 2026 Press Release Washington D.C. -  Congressman Fuller introduced the Securing Healthcare and Income Entitlements for Lawfully Domiciled Citizens Act, or the SHIELD Citizens Act, H.R. 9667, to keep federal welfare programs for citizens of the United States only, barring the programs for non-citizens. The bill amends the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act of 1996 to require citizenship for TANF, SNAP, Supplemental Security Income, Medicaid, federal housing assistance, WIC, and the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program. "Thirty years ago, this would have been a bipartisan issue, but this illustrates how far the radical left has shifted. Welfare programs funded by American tax dollars should not be the incentive, nor should they be available to non-citizens," said Congressman Fuller. Congressman Fuller Votes to Keep PFAS Cleanup Money Flowing and Keep the Government Funded by Passing H.R. 9770, the Continuing Appropriations Act | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Votes to Keep PFAS Cleanup Money Flowing and Keep the Government Funded by Passing H.R. 9770, the Continuing Appropriations Act July 21, 2026 Press Release WASHINGTON, D.C. Congressman Fuller voted for H.R. 9770, the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027, which holds federal funding at current levels through December 4 and keeps water infrastructure and emerging contaminant programs running while Congress finishes work on full-year appropriations. "My family has been in North Georgia for eight generations. I have sat in rooms in Northwest Georgia with people who are afraid of their own water," said Congressman Fuller. "This vote was not complicated. I voted to keep the cleanup money flowing into Northwest Georgia. 205 Democrats voted to shut it off and pick a shutdown fight six weeks before an election." Federal PFAS drinking water funding runs primarily through the Environmental Protection Agency, which would lose funding for essential programs had the bill not passed. Congressman Fuller Introduced a Constitutional Amendment to End Automatic Citizenship for Children Born in the United States to Illegal Immigrants | Congressman Clay Fuller Skip to main content Congressman Fuller Introduced a Constitutional Amendment to End Automatic Citizenship for Children Born in the United States to Illegal Immigrants June 30, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. — The Supreme Court ruled today to uphold birthright citizenship and strike down President Trump's executive order on the issue. Congressman Fuller responded by pointing to House Joint Resolution 172, the constitutional amendment he introduced on May 4 to end automatic citizenship for children born in the United States to illegal immigrants. "Citizenship in this country is the most valuable thing we have to give. It is not a prize for breaking our laws to get here. As a prosecutor, I saw the price that having an open border has forced on Northwest Georgia families, and I will keep fighting to protect American citizenship. The Supreme Court has refused to stop this invasion, so Congress must act. We owe it to our children and all future generations of Americans to NOT become Europe," said Congressman Fuller. House Joint Resolution 172 would end automatic citizenship for the children of illegal immigrants. The resolution was referred to the House Committee on the Judiciary.
